item.title: YYForce의 휴머노이드 로봇 및 VLA 훈련 과정, 공영방송인 미디어콥 ‘미팅 AI’ 프로그램에서 집중 조명 - 국민기자뉴스
item.description:
요약

  • 기술 기반 인력 관리 솔루션 및 통합시설관리 서비스를 제공하는 YYForce Inc.(나스닥: YFOR, 이하 ‘YYForce’ 또는 ‘회사’)는 자사가 추진 중인 휴머노이드 로봇 훈련 프로젝트가 싱가포르 미디어콥(Mediacorp)이 제작·방영한 TV 프로그램에서 집중 조명됐다고 발표했다.
  • 베테랑 방송 진행자 장하이제(Zhang Haijie)가 진행한 이번 프로그램은 새롭게 부상하는 휴머노이드 로봇 기술과 실제 상용화를 위한 로봇 훈련 과정을 심층적으로 소개하고, 이를 직접 체험하는 방식으로 구성됐다.
  • 본 보도자료에 포함된 미래예측진술에는 YYForce의 사업 전략과 2030 비전, 휴머노이드 로봇을 포함한 AI 및 로봇 솔루션의 개발·훈련·통합·상용화, 인간과 로봇의 협업, 고객 수요, 투자 우선순위, 사업 운영 목표 등에 관한 진술이 포함되며, 이에 국한되지 않는다.

본문

기술 기반 인력 관리 솔루션 및 통합시설관리 서비스를 제공하는 YYForce Inc.(나스닥: YFOR, 이하 ‘YYForce’ 또는 ‘회사’)는 자사가 추진 중인 휴머노이드 로봇 훈련 프로젝트가 싱가포르 미디어콥(Mediacorp)이 제작·방영한 TV 프로그램에서 집중 조명됐다고 발표했다.

해당 방송은 미디어콥 8월드(8world)의 기술·시사 프로그램인 ‘미팅 AI(Meeting AI, ‘遇见AI’)’에서 ‘AI는 한 번만 가르쳐도 배울 수 있을까?(Can AI Learn in Just One Lesson?, ‘AI一教就会？’)’라는 제목으로 방영됐다.

전체 방송 영상은 유튜브(https://youtu.be/QdH6VVlspYI)에서 시청할 수 있다.

베테랑 방송 진행자 장하이제(Zhang Haijie)가 진행한 이번 프로그램은 새롭게 부상하는 휴머노이드 로봇 기술과 실제 상용화를 위한 로봇 훈련 과정을 심층적으로 소개하고, 이를 직접 체험하는 방식으로 구성됐다. 방송에서 진행자는 유니트리(Unitree)의 G1 휴머노이드 로봇을 활용한 원격조작(teleoperation) 시연에 직접 참여했다. 이 과정에서 가상현실(VR) 헤드셋과 머리, 양손, 양발에 부착한 5개의 정밀 추적 센서가 사용됐다. 해당 시스템은 사람의 움직임과 이동 속도를 실시간으로 로봇에 그대로 반영하는 동시에 관절 각도, 운동학적 위치 정보, 카메라 영상 데이터를 기록한다. 이렇게 수집된 정보는 높은 정확도와 충실도를 갖춘 피지컬 AI(Physical AI) 훈련용 데이터셋을 구축하는 데 활용된다.

방송에서 시연된 주요 기술 및 훈련 과정:

- 인간 작업자의 시연 및 운동학적 데이터 기록(Human Demonstration & Kinematic Logging): 인간 작업자가 표준화된 물리적 작업을 반복적으로 시연하는 과정에서 로봇의 관절 구동 정보와 카메라 영상 데이터를 수집한다. 이 방식은 좌표 정보를 수동으로 지정하거나 태깅할 필요 없이 훈련 데이터를 확보할 수 있도록 한다.

- 데이터 정제 및 필터링(Data Cleaning & Filtering): 기록된 동작 궤적과 센서 데이터 스트림을 선별하고 정제해 작업 수행 과정에서 발생한 이상 동작이나 최적의 결과를 얻지 못한 시연 데이터를 제거한다.

- 비전·언어·행동(VLA) 모델 훈련(Vision-Language-Action Training): 방송에서 시연된 바와 같이 휴머노이드 로봇이 컵을 스스로 인식하고 집어 들어 이동시키는 작업을 수행하도록 훈련하는 데는 인간 작업자의 시연 40회와 데이터 정제 과정이 필요했다. 이후 첨단 VLA 모델을 활용해 약 8시간 동안 신경망을 훈련한 결과, 로봇이 해당 작업을 자율적으로 수행할 수 있게 됐다.

이번 방송은 현실 세계에서 작동하는 체화형 인공지능(Embodied AI)의 실제 구현 과정을 보여줬다. 특히 서비스 로봇이 정형화되지 않은 실제 상업 환경에서 효과적이고 안전하게 작동하기 위해서는 현장 작업자의 경험과 동작을 기반으로 한 체계적인 학습이 선행돼야 한다는 점을 강조했다.

실제 서비스 환경으로 로봇 기술 적용 확대

YYForce는 단순한 로봇 기술 시연을 넘어 실제 상업 환경에서 활용할 수 있는 실용적인 애플리케이션을 중심으로 로봇 사업 전략을 개발하고 있다. 회사는 호텔·숙박 서비스, 통합시설관리, 상업용 청소, 배송, 보안 및 기타 노동집약적 서비스 분야 전반에서 휴머노이드 로봇과 특수 목적 로봇의 활용 가능성을 모색하고 있다.

YYForce의 로봇 사업에는 호텔 객실 및 화장실 청소, 호텔·숙박 서비스 관련 업무 등을 수행하기 위한 휴머노이드 로봇 훈련과 데이터 수집이 포함된다. 이와 함께 청소, 배송 및 기타 운영 업무에 특화된 상업용 로봇의 활용도 추진하고 있다.

YYForce는 인간 근로자와 AI 기반 시스템 및 로봇 기술을 결합함으로써 새로운 인력 운영 모델을 구축할 수 있을 것으로 보고 있다. 이러한 모델에서는 기술이 반복적이고 표준화된 업무와 육체적 부담이 큰 작업을 지원하는 한편, 인간 근로자는 의사소통과 판단력, 고객과의 직접적인 상호작용이 필요한 업무에 집중할 수 있게 된다.

인간과 로봇의 협업을 위한 인프라 구축

YYForce는 실제 서비스 환경에서 로봇 기술의 도입과 활용을 확대하기 위한 역량을 개발하고 있다. 회사는 싱가포르에 로봇 시연 및 훈련 시설을 구축했으며, 이곳에서 휴머노이드 로봇과 특수 목적 서비스 로봇을 선보이고 다양한 운영 환경에 맞춰 훈련하고 평가할 수 있도록 했다.

이러한 활동은 로봇 기술을 기존 인력 관리 및 시설관리 운영 체계에 효과적으로 통합할 수 있는 방안을 파악하는 동시에, 향후 로봇의 실제 현장 배치에 필요한 전문 역량과 운영 프로세스를 개발하기 위한 것이다.

YYForce의 최고경영자(CEO)인 마이크 푸(Mike Fu)는 “미디어콥(Mediacorp) 방송을 통해 더 많은 시청자에게 로봇 기술이 개념적 단계에서 실제 활용 단계로 얼마나 빠르게 발전하고 있는지 보여줄 수 있게 됐다. 이번 방송은 피지컬 AI(Physical AI)의 실제 구현 과정을 보여줬다. 로봇이 상업 환경에서 안정적으로 작동하기 위해서는 무엇보다 인간의 경험을 직접 학습하는 과정이 선행돼야 한다는 점을 확인할 수 있었다”고 말했다.

이어 “우리의 비전은 로봇으로 인간을 대체하는 것이 아니다. 우리는 인간과 AI, 휴머노이드 로봇, 특수 목적 서비스 로봇이 각자의 강점을 가장 효과적으로 발휘할 수 있는 업무를 수행하면서 서로 협력하는 새로운 운영 모델을 구축하고자 한다”고 밝혔다.

마이크 푸 CEO는 “호텔·숙박 서비스와 시설관리 분야는 반복적이고 육체적인 작업뿐 아니라 다양한 고객 서비스 업무가 이루어지는 만큼, 이러한 역량을 개발하기에 적합한 실제 현장 환경을 제공한다. 이처럼 현장 중심의 실습형 훈련 방식은 ‘YYForce 2030 비전(YYForce 2030 Vision)’의 핵심 요소다. 우리는 미래의 업무 환경을 향해 ‘함께 전진한다(Forging Forward Together)’는 목표 아래 이러한 노력을 지속해 나갈 것”이라고 덧붙였다.

item.title: It's the Mighty Morphin' Quadrotors?! - IEEE Spectrum
item.description:
요약

  • Video Friday is your weekly selection of awesome robotics videos, collected by your friends at IEEE Spectrum robotics.
  • We also post a weekly calendar of upcoming robotics events for the next few months.
  • Walden Robotics is a full-stack company building both the hardware and physical AI for general-purpose manufacturing robots.

본문

Video Friday is your weekly selection of awesome robotics videos, collected by your friends at IEEE Spectrum robotics. We also post a weekly calendar of upcoming robotics events for the next few months. Please send us your events for inclusion.

Humanoids 2026: 6–9 December 2026, SANTA CLARA, CA

Enjoy today’s videos!

Drones navigating cluttered spaces often encounter openings narrower than their bodies. We present a design method that jointly optimizes a quadrotor’s geometry and how its two side arms bend on contact. The resulting prototype folds from 31.3 cm to 14.1 cm wide on contact and flies through a 15 cm opening.

[ Paper ] via [ Autonomous Robots Lab ]

Thanks, Kostas!

TeCoBots are soft, snake-like robots that can work alone and can also grab onto each other to form chains, loops and branches, building a new body for each task. A single robot can inch like a worm, roll across gravel and grass, climb inside a pipe and lift a 2.5-liter water bottle. The claw it uses to grab objects is the same one it uses to grab another robot, so linking up needs no extra docking hardware. Linked together, the robots do things none can do alone.

Thanks, Mahmud!

AHEADance is a humanoid robot that makes up its dance as the music plays. It listens to the song as it streams in, takes a guess at what the next half second of music will sound like, and moves to match, in the style of whatever is playing. When the music stops, it stands still and waits, and when the music comes back, so does the dancing. Curious what it would do with your favourite song? Play it through the live demo on our project page and watch the robot have a go.

Thanks, Chengxu!

I am... Not at all sure how I feel about this.

Most affordable dexterous hands use tendons, and anyone who has worked with them knows the pain of re-tensioning and replacing them. I wanted to see whether rigid linkages could get you human-like dexterity without that maintenance, and so far the answer looks like yes. Each finger has three actuated degrees of freedom, the hand can grasp and manipulate a wide range of objects, and the whole thing is 3D-printed for less than $650 in parts.

I’m not sure that this is an entirely faithful representation of the capabilities of this robot goose, but it’s so cute that we’ll let it slide. For now.

[ Robot Works ]

You’ve seen data-collection gloves. You’ve seen teleoperation gloves. But this is different. What if the glove itself IS the robot hand?

Can we treat a flapping wing like a rotary wing? In our latest IEEE [Robotics and Automation Letters] work, we developed CROBAT, a fully actuated quad-thopter with wing thrust vectoring, enabling independent position and attitude control. The robot demonstrates full-pose flapping flight and tilted perching, showing a pathway toward flapping-wing robots that go beyond navigation toward physical interaction.

item.title: Leaky Buckets, Skeptics at the Helm and Why Humanoid Robots Aren’t the Future: IndustryWeek’s Weekly Review - IndustryWeek

요약

본문

Leaky Buckets, Skeptics at the Helm and Why Humanoid Robots Aren’t the Future: IndustryWeek’s Weekly Review

Welcome to IndustryWeek’s Weekly review, where we share the most-consumed content at industryweek.com over the previous seven days. Without further ado, here are the Top 10.

Demand and Optimism Are Rising, So It's Time to Fix the Leaks in Your Bucket: A Wipfli survey shows strong revenue growth expectations and hiring intentions for 2027. With costs still a challenge, the quality of new business and profits is becoming a greater priority.

3 Questions That Saved Lego: The Importance of Leaders As Skeptics: If systematically challenging assumptions is so valuable, why don't leaders make it standard operating procedure?

Battery Scrap Has Become a Critical Resource for US Manufacturers: Collecting and processing these materials—including the scrap known as “black mass”—can provide domestic sources of materials that would otherwise be exported for processing.

Effective Leader Standard Work Requires Consistency, Discipline: Organizations rarely become more consistent or disciplined if their leadership isn't. Leader standard work builds consistent, explicit leadership routines that support a continuous improvement culture. Lasting discipline depends on connecting routines to a meaningful purpose.

Plan, Do, Check, Act (PDCA): Focus on the Learning: Why you should use Plan, Do, Check, Act as a learning cycle for solving problems, rather than as a checklist for implementing solutions.

Humanoid Robots Aren't the Future of Manufacturing AI: Digital twins and predictive maintenance are technologies quietly doing the work in factories.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns: Departure follows revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.

2026 IW U.S. 500: Top Building Products Manufacturers (slideshow): A weaker residential end market was a nearly universal challenge cited by the IW 500’s building products manufacturers.

Podcast: How to Build a Successful Veteran Hiring and Retention Program: In this episode of Great Question: A Manufacturing Podcast, Scott Gromer of Mesa Power Solutions explains how the DoD SkillBridge program was essential for recruiting skilled veteran workers.

23 AI Pilots and No Results? You've Got a Problem: It's an organizational problem, and the companies solving it are building something bigger than AI.

item.title: New underwater robot dives 328 feet deep to spot hull damage before it sinks your trip - Interesting Engineering
item.description:
요약

  • A Chinese underwater robot that lets boat owners inspect propellers, check hull damage, and explore submerged areas without getting wet is now available for $3,499.
  • Developed by underwater robotics specialist QYSEA, the FIFISH V6 EXPERT is a tethered remotely operated vehicle (ROV) with a modular design that includes detachable components for its motor, lighting, camera, and battery.
  • The system combines 4K cameras, multidirectional movement, and an optional robotic arm to capture footage and handle small objects underwater.

본문

A Chinese underwater robot that lets boat owners inspect propellers, check hull damage, and explore submerged areas without getting wet is now available for $3,499.

Developed by underwater robotics specialist QYSEA, the FIFISH V6 EXPERT is a tethered remotely operated vehicle (ROV) with a modular design that includes detachable components for its motor, lighting, camera, and battery.

The system combines 4K cameras, multidirectional movement, and an optional robotic arm to capture footage and handle small objects underwater.

The system allows users to investigate potential damage, check for tangled ropes, and examine submerged objects from the surface.

Robotic diving expert

Designed to operate in environments that are difficult or unsafe for divers to access, the ROV combines a high-definition camera, six degrees of freedom (6-DOF) movement, powerful LED lighting, and compatibility with several underwater tools. It can descend to depths of up to 100 meters (328 feet), allowing users to examine boat hulls, propellers, underwater structures, and other submerged objects.

The robot measures 38.3 centimeters long, 33.1 centimeters wide, and 14.3 centimeters high. It weighs approximately 4.6 kilograms (10.14 pounds), making it relatively compact for transportation and deployment. Its propulsion system uses multiple thrusters to provide movement in six directions: forward and backward, left and right, and up and down. It can also rotate through 360 degrees in yaw, pitch, and roll, allowing it to change orientation without needing to turn around. QYSEA lists its maximum speed at 3 knots (1.5 meters per second).

More from AI and Robotics

The V6 EXPERT uses a 1/2.3-inch Sony CMOS image sensor with 12-megapixel resolution and an f/2.5 lens. Its camera offers a 166-degree field of view above water and a 96-degree field of view underwater. It can record 4K video at 25 or 30 frames per second, while 1080p footage can be captured at up to 120 frames per second.

To improve visibility in dark underwater environments, the ROV carries two LED lights producing a combined 6,000 lumens. The lights have a 5,500K color temperature and a 120-degree beam angle. Users can save footage and photographs using its removable microSD storage system, which comes with a 128GB card and supports cards up to 256GB according to QYSEA’s current specifications.

Precision diving technology

The robot also incorporates onboard sensors to help maintain its position and orientation underwater. These include a gyroscope, accelerometer, magnetometer, depth sensor, and temperature sensor.

According to the firm, its depth-lock function can maintain a selected depth with an accuracy of approximately ±1 centimeter, helping the vehicle remain steady while inspecting a particular section of a boat or underwater structure. Other intelligent features include Vision Lock, Diver Tracking, and Q-STEADY 2.0 stabilization technology. Arm+1

item.title: 금속탐지기 든 휴머노이드, 지뢰밭 첫발 대신 내딛는다 - 데일리방산
item.description:
요약

  • 폭발물이 의심되는 지면을 수색하는 일은 사람을 위험에 빠뜨린다.
  • 스카이락랩스(Skylark Labs)가 일반 휴대용 금속탐지기를 들고 이 수색을 대신 수행하는 휴머노이드를 시연했다.
  • EOD 장비 공급업체 관계자는 "고객들은 이미 자신의 탐지기를 소유하고 신뢰한다"며 "전문가에게서 수색 방법을 배운 로봇이 같은 장비로 그 임무를 수행하면, 사람에게 더 많은 일을 떠넘기지 않으면서 가장 위험한 순간에서 사람을 빼낼 수 있다"고 말했다.

본문

폭발물이 의심되는 지면을 수색하는 일은 사람을 위험에 빠뜨린다. 스카이락랩스(Skylark Labs)가 일반 휴대용 금속탐지기를 들고 이 수색을 대신 수행하는 휴머노이드를 시연했다.

20일(현지시간) 브레이킹디펜스에 따르면 이 로봇은 금속탐지기로 지면을 훑고, 경보음이 울리면 반응하는 일련의 과정을 사람의 감독 아래 수행한다. 목표는 폭발물처리(EOD) 전문가가 수색을 지휘·평가하는 동안 의심 위험물에서 더 멀리 떨어져 있게 하는 것이다.

EOD 장비 공급업체를 대상으로 진행된 실험에서 로봇은 탐지기를 집어 들고 지정된 수색 구역을 훑은 뒤, 경보음이 울리자 멈춰 섰다가 뒤로 물러섰다. 각 단계마다 별도의 명령 없이 이 순서를 스스로 수행했다.

스카이락은 시각·음향 피드백이 로봇의 임무 수행을 이끌었다고 설명했다. 탐지기의 경보음이 로봇의 다음 행동을 결정하는 입력값이 돼, 기계가 감지한 것과 행동한 것을 연결했다는 것이다. 회사가 공개한 영상에는 휴머노이드가 같은 수색을 수행하는 사람 옆에서 야외 지면을 훑는 모습이 담겼다.

EOD 장비 공급업체 관계자는 "고객들은 이미 자신의 탐지기를 소유하고 신뢰한다"며 "전문가에게서 수색 방법을 배운 로봇이 같은 장비로 그 임무를 수행하면, 사람에게 더 많은 일을 떠넘기지 않으면서 가장 위험한 순간에서 사람을 빼낼 수 있다"고 말했다.

위협은 지속적이다. 무장폭력대응기구(AOAV)는 2015년부터 2024년까지 94개국에서 1만376건의 급조폭발물(IED) 사건을 기록했으며, 이로 인한 민간인 사상자는 8만3529명에 달한다고 집계했다. 의심 장치는 이동을 막고 접근을 제한하며 인력을 다른 곳으로 돌리게 만들기도 한다.

EOD 팀은 이미 로봇에 의존하고 있다. 미 공군은 2022년부터 조작자가 원격으로 통제하는 궤도형 기계인 L3해리스 T7 시스템 170대를 배치하기 시작했다. 스카이락은 이와 달리 사람이 모든 움직임을 지시하지 않아도 할당된 수색을 수행하는 휴머노이드를 추구하고 있다.

휴머노이드 형태는 이 접근법의 핵심이다. 손과 팔 길이, 자세 덕분에 EOD 팀이 이미 휴대하는 탐지기를 포함해 사람용으로 설계된 장비를 그대로 다룰 수 있다. 이런 도구 사용법을 학습하면 로봇에 맞춰 장비를 다시 설계할 필요가 줄어든다. 기대되는 실질적 효과는 기계를 지시하는 시간을 줄이고, 수색 최전선에서의 인체 노출을 줄이는 것이다.

학습 능력은 스카이락의 '지속적 현장 적응 모델'(CFAM)이 제공한다. 전문가가 익숙한 장비를 다루고 수색을 수행하는 방법을 시연하면 된다. 스카이락은 탐지기 수색 기술을 몇 분간의 인간 시연만으로 가르쳤다고 밝혔다. 이 모델은 별도의 재학습 주기 없이 로봇이 작업하는 동안 기기에서 계속 적응하도록 설계됐다.

CFAM은 실제 조작 시험에서 표준 모델보다 약 30% 높은 임무 성공률을 기록했다. 별도 평가에서는 훈련 데이터의 40%만으로 표준 모델과 동등한 성능을 냈다. 또한 이전 능력의 손실을 거의 일으키지 않으면서 새로운 기술을 학습했다. 다만 새로운 수색 조건에서의 성능은 아직 시험 중이다.

미 해병대 예비역 중장이자 펜타곤 합동인공지능센터(JAIC) 전 소장, 스카이락랩스 국방자문위원회 위원인 마이클 S. 그로엔은 "수색되지 않은 지면에 처음 내딛는 발걸음이 가장 큰 위험을 안고 있다"며 "기계가 미지의 것을 식별하면서 인간의 위험을 줄일 수 있다면, 전문적 판단은 가장 복잡한 도전 과제에만 남겨둘 수 있다"고 말했다.

그는 "이는 기계 감지와 인간 판단을 즉시 결합해 어느 한쪽도 단독으로는 달성할 수 없는 통합적 이해를 얻을 수 있을 때만 가능하다"고 덧붙였다.

이번에 시연된 작업은 탐지 지원이다. 물리적 처리와 폐기는 여전히 개발 목표로 남아 있다. 휴머노이드의 가치는 전문가가 수색되지 않은 지면에 가장 먼저 들어서는 대신, 더 먼 거리에서 감독할 수 있을 만큼 정의된 수색을 안정적으로 수행하는 데 달려 있다.

스카이락랩스의 아마르조트 싱 창업자 겸 최고경영자(CEO)는 "우리의 사명은 휴머노이드를 포함한 기계가 폭발물처리 임무를 독립적으로 수행해 사람을 잠재적 치명 위협에서 멀어지게 하는 것"이라며 "이 기계들이 효율적으로 학습하고 낯선 물체·지형·변화하는 조건에 적응하도록 하는 AI 두뇌를 구축하고 있으며, 복잡한 EOD 작전에서 신뢰할 수 있고 효과적으로 만드는 것이 목표"라고 밝혔다.

스카이락의 장기 목표는 여러 휴머노이드가 함께 작업하는 팀이다. 여러 기계를 조율하는 프레임워크인 '하이브'(Hive)는 이미 미국·인도·중동의 석유·가스 작업에 배치돼 있다. 이를 EOD에 적용하면 로봇들이 수색 구역을 나누고, 발견 사항을 공유하고, 조건이 바뀌면 작업을 넘겨받으며 한 명의 전문가가 팀 전체를 감독할 수 있게 된다.

목표는 기계를 먼저 보내되, 전문가가 통제권을 계속 쥐게 하는 것이다.

출처: 데일리방산

item.title: US firm unveils Phantom MKII battlefield humanoid robot with bigger payload, tougher build - Interesting Engineering
item.description:
요약

  • San Francisco-based robotics startup Foundation Future Industries has unveiled its second-generation humanoid robot, the Phantom MKII, alongside an upgraded artificial intelligence control system called Cortex II.
  • Engineered for heavy industrial work and military support roles, the new bipedal platform is designed to haul up to 200 pounds (91 kilograms) while walking through rain, snow, and dust.
  • While most commercial humanoids operate in controlled environments, Foundation has explicitly pursued dual-use defense and rugged field applications, aiming to begin early production of the MKII in the San Francisco Bay Area in early 2027.

본문

San Francisco-based robotics startup Foundation Future Industries has unveiled its second-generation humanoid robot, the Phantom MKII, alongside an upgraded artificial intelligence control system called Cortex II.

Engineered for heavy industrial work and military support roles, the new bipedal platform is designed to haul up to 200 pounds (91 kilograms) while walking through rain, snow, and dust.

Founded in 2024 by CEO Sankaet Pathak and former U.S. Marine Corps officer Mike LeBlanc, Foundation has positioned itself differently from competitors focused solely on indoor warehouse or factory automation. While most commercial humanoids operate in controlled environments, Foundation has explicitly pursued dual-use defense and rugged field applications, aiming to begin early production of the MKII in the San Francisco Bay Area in early 2027.

Weatherproofing, payload gains, and Cortex II

According to an interview with Pathak published by Fast Company on November 18, 2026, the Phantom MKII directly addresses hardware bottlenecks uncovered during early field trials of its predecessor, the Phantom MK-1. Earlier testing highlighted limitations in battery runtime, waterproofing, and lifting capacity. These constraints restricted how long the first-generation robot could operate outdoors.

To overcome those hurdles, engineers redesigned the Phantom MKII with environmental sealing against precipitation and dust, higher-load actuators capable of supporting a 200-pound walking payload, and a simplified assembly that Pathak claims cuts the bill-of-materials cost in half.

On the software side, the companion Cortex II control system is built to learn physical tasks by observing human demonstrations, requiring as few as 60 examples for certain operations rather than extensive custom programming.

More from AI and Robotics

Lessons from Ukraine trials and battlefield philosophy

The hardware overhaul follows Foundation’s high-profile push to test humanoid robotics in active conflict zones. Earlier in 2026, the company drew widespread attention after sending two Phantom MK-1 units to Ukraine for non-combat logistics and reconnaissance evaluations, though independent reporting later noted disagreements over how extensively the prototypes operated on the ground.

Those trials reinforced the need for fall recovery, ruggedized joints, and longer endurance before humanoids can handle frontline supply runs or hazard detection. Unlike robotics developers that strictly prohibit military uses, Foundation openly embraces defense deployment under a “human-in-the-loop” framework, meaning human operators retain final authority over any use of force.

item.title: Skylark Labs demonstrates humanoid search for explosive hazards - Breaking Defense
item.description:
요약

  • Searching suspected explosive ground puts people in danger.
  • Skylark Labs has demonstrated a humanoid that can take on that search with a standard handheld metal detector—sweeping the ground and responding to its alert under human supervision.
  • The aim is to keep explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) specialists farther from suspected hazards while they direct and assess the search.

본문

Searching suspected explosive ground puts people in danger. Skylark Labs has demonstrated a humanoid that can take on that search with a standard handheld metal detector—sweeping the ground and responding to its alert under human supervision. The aim is to keep explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) specialists farther from suspected hazards while they direct and assess the search.

In an experiment conducted for an EOD supplier, the robot picked up the detector, swept a designated search area and stopped and backed off when it sounded. It carried out the sequence without a separate command for each step.

Skylark says visual and audio feedback guided the robot through the task. The detector’s beep became an input to its next action, connecting what the machine sensed with what it did. Company footage shows the humanoid sweeping outdoors alongside a person performing the same search. The demo footage can be seen here.

“Our customers already own and trust their detectors. A robot that learns the search from the specialists who do it, and then runs it with that same equipment, takes people out of the most dangerous moments without handing them more work.”

EOD supplier representative

The threat is persistent. Action on Armed Violence recorded 10,376 IED incidents across 94 countries between 2015 and 2024, causing 83,529 civilian deaths and injuries. Suspected devices can also halt movement, restrict access and divert personnel.

EOD teams already rely on robots. In 2022, the U.S. Air Force began fielding 170 L3Harris T7 systems: tracked machines controlled by an operator. Skylark is pursuing a humanoid that carries out an assigned search without requiring a person to direct each movement.

The humanoid form is central to that approach. Its hands, reach and posture let it work with equipment designed for people, including the detectors EOD teams already carry. Learning to use those tools reduces the need to redesign equipment around a robot. The intended payoff is practical: less time spent directing a machine, and less human exposure at the front of the search.

Skylark’s Continual Field-Adaptive Models, or CFAMs, provide the learning capability. Specialists demonstrate how to handle familiar equipment and carry out a search. Skylark says the detector-search skill was taught through a few minutes of human demonstration. The models are designed to keep adapting on the device as the robot works, without a separate retraining cycle.

CFAM delivered about 30% higher task success than a standard model in a real-world manipulation test. In a separate evaluation, it matched a standard model’s performance using just 40% of the training data. It also learned new skills with little loss of earlier capabilities. Performance in new search conditions is still being tested.

item.title: China deploys 65-pound robot to insulate nearly 100-foot live power line in 15 minutes - Interesting Engineering
item.description:
요약

  • Humans climbing up electric poles to carry out repair work could soon be a thing of the past in China.
  • That shift may be closer than expected, thanks to robots developed by the state-owned power supply company in Jiangsu province.
  • State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company recently demonstrated the technology, in which robots placed insulating material on live overhead power lines without turning off the electricity.

본문

Humans climbing up electric poles to carry out repair work could soon be a thing of the past in China.

That shift may be closer than expected, thanks to robots developed by the state-owned power supply company in Jiangsu province.

State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company recently demonstrated the technology, in which robots placed insulating material on live overhead power lines without turning off the electricity.

By allowing maintenance to be carried out while the grid remained energized, the installation did not require shutting down the power supply, providing residents with seamless electricity as the upgrade work was ongoing.

Safely sleeving power lines

According to the company, the newly developed robots, which weigh a little more than 65 pounds (less than 30 kilograms), completed the task of sleeving a 30-meter power line in just 15 minutes.

The Chinese power supplier said the robots could be adapted to upgrade power distribution networks of 35 kilovolts (kV) and below, potentially extending the technology to a wider range of maintenance projects.

To carry out the task, the robot can automatically access power lines, position itself using its machine vision feature, and accurately move and position the insulating sleeve before installation using its servo motors. At the same time, the machine is well protected from the strong electromagnetic environment, steering clear of any electrical shock.

More from AI and Robotics

Human operator aids deployment

Although the robot performs most of the physical work on its own, it does not operate entirely without human involvement.

A human operator remains on the ground and controls or supervises the robot using a remote-control device, computer, or control console.

Once remotely deployed by an operator, the robot autonomously travels along energized power lines, installs insulating sleeves with precise alignment, and uses onboard sensors to verify installation quality in real time.

According to the company, the pilot was conducted safely without affecting electricity use for consumers. Moreover, a later on-site inspection of the power lines showed that the sleeves were installed securely and met the required docking accuracy, meaning each sleeve was correctly connected, the company said in its press statement.

Edge over manual maintenance

The successful demonstration also highlighted the broader advantages of replacing conventional maintenance methods with robotic systems.

The company said the exercise shows the equipment effectively avoids the safety risks of high-altitude work while preventing power outages, suggesting a shift away from traditional insulation upgrades that rely heavily on manual pole climbing and bucket truck operations.

Moreover, such conventional methods are often unsuitable for residential areas with narrow alleys and also pose additional safety risks.

item.title: Siemens and AGIBOT Show AI Agent That Designs 3D Printed Humanoid Robot Grippers from a Text Prompt - 3D Printing Industry
item.description:
요약

  • Siemens is building an end-to-end Digital Thread for additive manufacturing (AM).
  • The system runs on Industrial AI and is meant to carry the requirements of each product from design through to production.
  • On the engineering side, an AI agent handles each step from adapting the design and validating it virtually to preparing it for manufacturing.

본문

Siemens is building an end-to-end Digital Thread for additive manufacturing (AM). The system runs on Industrial AI and is meant to carry the requirements of each product from design through to production. The company says the Digital Thread connects, for the first time, agentic, prompt-based engineering with an adaptive production environment. On the engineering side, an AI agent handles each step from adapting the design and validating it virtually to preparing it for manufacturing. A planned adaptive production cell will then take the approach onto the factory floor.

Designing a Gripper from a Text Description

Siemens and AGIBOT demonstrate the engineering workflow using a gripper for a humanoid robot. The user starts by describing the object to be handled and the task the robot needs to perform. From that input, the AI agent picks a suitable gripper type, adapts its geometry in Siemens’ Designcenter, simulates it, and validates the robot interface and handling. MCP integration lets the agent use functions of the engineering software and coordinate the work steps. The workflow then prepares the data for AM.

The result is a gripper built for a specific application, which can be validated virtually and prepared for AM before production begins. Siemens says the approach could open complex engineering workflows to more users, because they would no longer need to work directly with each engineering tool and process step. The company is exhibiting the workflow at Formnext 2026 in Frankfurt (Hall 12.1, Booth D119).

“Instead of manually designing variants in a time-consuming process, agentic workflows can orchestrate engineering tasks based on specific requirements. Additive manufacturing is the ideal complement because it enables individual designs to be flexibly turned into physical components. The next step is production that can respond just as flexibly to this variety,” said Karsten Heuser, Vice President Additive Manufacturing at Siemens.

Adaptive Production Cell in Erlangen

More product variants put new demands on the production steps that follow design. Siemens is working with EOS and AM Solutions on an adaptive production cell at its Electronics Factory in Erlangen. The cell is designed to combine AM, automation and software in an integrated process chain. The goal is to handle different components and production requirements while setting up repeatable, scalable production processes.

“The next stage in the evolution of Industry 4.0 is Industrial AI: the shift from connected and automated factories to intelligent, adaptive manufacturing,” said Marie Niehaus-Langer, CEO of EOS. “Together, we want to advance an independent European approach to the future of manufacturing and translate technological excellence into industrial competitiveness, resilience, and sovereignty.”

Post-processing has been part of the cell’s design from the outset.

item.title: 구미 로봇산업 포럼서 휴머노이드 제조현장 적용 방안 논의 - 경북일보
item.description:
요약

  • 구미코에 산학연 관계자 100여 명 참석…기술 표준화 논의
  • 구미시, 전자·반도체 제조 기반 활용해 로봇 핵심부품 육성
  • 휴머노이드와 피지컬 인공지능(AI) 기술이 제조업의 새로운 성장 동력으로 부상하면서 지역 제조기반을 로봇산업과 연결하기 위한 전략 마련에 나선 것이다.

본문

구미코에 산학연 관계자 100여 명 참석…기술 표준화 논의

구미시, 전자·반도체 제조 기반 활용해 로봇 핵심부품 육성

구미 로봇산업 육성을 위한 산학연 협력 논의가 본격화하고 있다. 휴머노이드와 피지컬 인공지능(AI) 기술이 제조업의 새로운 성장 동력으로 부상하면서 지역 제조기반을 로봇산업과 연결하기 위한 전략 마련에 나선 것이다.

구미시는 19일 구미코에서 서울대와 레인보우로보틱스 등 국내 대학·기업·연구기관 관계자 100여 명이 참석한 가운데 ‘구미 로봇산업 생태계 활성화 포럼’을 개최했다.

구미전자정보기술원과 서울대 정밀기계설계공동연구소가 공동 주최한 이번 포럼에서는 국내외 AI·로봇산업 정책과 기술 동향, 휴머노이드 기술의 제조현장 적용, 산업 표준화 등이 주요 의제로 다뤄졌다.

서울대 안성훈 교수는 AI·로봇산업 동향을, 레인보우로보틱스 허정우 연구소장은 피지컬 AI 기반 기술 발전 방향을 발표했다. 한국AI·로봇산업협회 전한구 본부장도 산업 정책과 기술 표준화 과제를 소개했다.

이어 한국기계연구원과 한국로봇융합연구원 등 전문가들이 참여한 토론에서는 구미 제조업의 로봇산업 전환 가능성과 지역 기업의 참여 확대 방안이 논의됐다. 참석자들은 HT로보틱스와 엘씨텍 등 지역 로봇기업을 방문해 기술 개발 현황과 제조현장의 수요도 살폈다.

구미시는 이번 포럼을 지역 산업기반과 로봇 기술을 연결하는 계기로 삼겠다는 구상이다. 구미국가산업단지의 전자·반도체 제조 역량을 활용해 휴머노이드 핵심부품과 첨단 로봇 제조 분야를 육성하고, 지역 기업의 기술 개발과 사업화를 지원한다는 계획이다.

특히 삼성의 구미 투자계획과 대구·경북(구미·포항) 로봇 국가첨단전략산업 특화단지 공동 지정을 산업 생태계 확대의 기반으로 보고 있다. 산학연 공동 연구개발(R&D), 핵심부품 국산화, 실증·사업화 지원과 국책사업 발굴을 통해 지역 기업의 로봇산업 진입을 유도하고 공급망 경쟁력을 높이는 데 초점을 맞추고 있다.

다만 로봇산업 생태계가 지역에 뿌리내리려면 투자와 특화단지 지정을 넘어 핵심부품 기술 확보, 전문인력 양성, 지역 기업의 실제 사업 참여로 이어지는 후속 전략이 필요하다.

김장호 구미시장은 “산학연 협력을 강화해 핵심기술 개발과 실증·사업화를 지원하고 지역 기업의 경쟁력을 높이겠다”고 말했다.

출처: 경북일보

본문

AAEON Debuts First Jetson Thor Platform Box PC, Targeting Humanoid Robot Edge AI Opportunity

Industrial PC maker AAEON Technology (6579.TW) on the 20th unveiled its first embedded Box PC built on the NVIDIA Jetson Thor platform, the "BOXER-8741AI," touting AI computing performance of up to 2,070 FP4 TFLOPS and robot-specific I/O interfaces. The product directly targets emerging applications such as industrial-grade humanoid robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and service robots, adding another hardware tool to the company's Physical AI ambitions that it has been actively building in recent years.

AAEON said the BOXER-8741AI is equipped with the NVIDIA Jetson T5000 module, featuring a 14-core Arm Neoverse-V3AE CPU and 128GB of LPDDR5X memory, and integrates a 2,560-core GPU based on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture along with fifth-generation Tensor Cores. Compared with the previous-generation NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the new model delivers up to 7.5 times higher AI computing performance and 3.5 times better energy efficiency, offering clear advantages in compute power and power consumption for edge AI scenarios that require real-time processing of large volumes of sensor data at the endpoint.

In terms of connectivity, the new product features two 10GbE and four 5GbE RJ-45 network ports, enabling simultaneous connection to multiple high-bandwidth sensor devices. To address the needs of distributed actuator communication, sensor connectivity, and real-time monitoring in humanoid robots, the system also provides three DB-9 ports supporting dual-channel CAN FD, RS-232, RS-485, and 8-bit GPIO interfaces. It also includes four USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports and M.2 M-Key, B-Key, and E-Key expansion slots for installing NVMe storage devices, 4G/5G/LTE and Wi-Fi/BT wireless communication modules, along with a built-in Nano SIM card slot, allowing developers to flexibly expand according to field requirements.

The chassis design continues AAEON's industrial-grade approach in the AI@Edge series. The BOXER-8741AI measures 240mm × 164.8mm × 105.1mm, supports a wide operating temperature range of -20°C to 60°C, accepts a wide 19V to 48V power input via a 2-pin terminal block connector, and offers shock and vibration resistance, making it suitable for deployment in dynamic, high-vibration environments such as industrial robots.

On the software side, the model supports NVIDIA JetPack 7 and later versions, and can run NVIDIA's software stacks built for Physical AI, including the robotics development platform NVIDIA Isaac, NVIDIA Metropolis for Visual Agentic AI, and NVIDIA Holoscan designed specifically for sensor data processing, helping developers accelerate the construction of next-generation intelligent robots and edge AI solutions.

The following are the main specifications of the BOXER-8741AI:

| Item | Specification |

| Compute Module | NVIDIA Jetson T5000 |

| CPU | 14-core Arm Neoverse-V3AE |

| GPU | 2,560-core Blackwell architecture GPU, fifth-generation Tensor Cores |

item.title: Robot Motor Driver Chips: Camera Chipmaker Dongwoon Anatech Plans 48V Parts, Names No Specs - Tech Times
item.description:
요약

  • Buyers evaluating robot motor driver chips should read the announcement as a statement of intent, not a product launch.
  • The Korean business outlet Asia Economy reported on Nov. 16 that Dongwoon has set up an Automotive and Robotics (A&R) Group led by Jin Park. Park said the company wants to become a key chip supplier that turns AI decisions into movement.
  • Dongwoon also says that core design assets can be reused across mobile, automotive and robotics platforms, at a share above 50 percent, but it has not shown how it measured that figure.

본문

Dongwoon Anatech, the South Korean chipmaker best known for smartphone camera lens drivers, announced at 11 a.m. ET on Nov. 19 that it is developing 48V motor drivers, 48V eFuses and gate drivers for robots running on 12V and 48V power systems, but it gave no part numbers, sampling dates, revenue targets or named customers. The distance to cover is large: the company's published autofocus drivers list supply voltages of 2.3V to 3.6V and currents of roughly 100 to 120 milliamps, while humanoid joints increasingly run on 48V buses, a step of about 13 to 21 times in voltage, according to Allegro's robotics 48V white paper.

Buyers evaluating robot motor driver chips should read the announcement as a statement of intent, not a product launch. The Korean business outlet Asia Economy reported on Nov. 16 that Dongwoon has set up an Automotive and Robotics (A&R) Group led by Jin Park. Park said the company wants to become a key chip supplier that turns AI decisions into movement. Dongwoon also says that core design assets can be reused across mobile, automotive and robotics platforms, at a share above 50 percent, but it has not shown how it measured that figure.

Voice-Coil Autofocus Drivers Run on Single-Digit Volts; Robot Joints Need Three-Phase Power at 48V

A smartphone autofocus driver steers one coil. A voice coil motor is a coil that moves in a magnetic field, and its driver mostly sets the current through that single coil. A robot joint is a different machine: a brushless motor, usually permanent-magnet synchronous, in which a controller must switch three sets of windings in step with the rotor's position.

That job runs on field-oriented control, which splits motor current into torque and flux components with Clarke and Park mathematical transforms and repeats the calculation every pulse-width-modulation cycle, typically above 10 kilohertz in high-performance drives. Dongwoon's pitch is that the precision it used to move smartphone lenses carries over to joint control, but its listed autofocus drivers top out at 3.6V and do not switch a power bridge at 48V. What plausibly carries over is sensing and control logic. The power stage, gate drive, protection and safety certification are new work, and Dongwoon's release lists the drivers, eFuses and gate drivers as products still in development.

The control stakes are high. Electronic Design reported that a robot taking a single step can coordinate as many as 40 motor joints. TI's own reference design shows the scale of the hardware: it drives a 48V, 1 kilowatt humanoid joint motor from a board 70 millimeters (2.8 in) across, using three 100V, 60A gallium-nitride power stages.

item.title: World’s robotics leaders to gather in Germany in race to put AI to work - The European Magazine
item.description:
요약

  • World’s robotics leaders to gather in Germany in race to put AI to work
  • From humanoid factory workers to robots that learn new tasks, some of the biggest names in artificial intelligence and robotics are heading to Germany next week to tackle the obstacles standing between experimental machines and widespread industrial use
  • Some of the world’s leading robotics and AI firms will gather in Germany next week for a major international conference aimed at bringing humanoid robots out of the laboratory and into everyday industrial use.

본문

World’s robotics leaders to gather in Germany in race to put AI to work

- News, Technology

From humanoid factory workers to robots that learn new tasks, some of the biggest names in artificial intelligence and robotics are heading to Germany next week to tackle the obstacles standing between experimental machines and widespread industrial use

Some of the world’s leading robotics and AI firms will gather in Germany next week for a major international conference aimed at bringing humanoid robots out of the laboratory and into everyday industrial use.

The Advanced Robotics Conference 2026 (ARC) will bring together technology developers, manufacturers and researchers to examine how the latest generation of intelligent machines can be made reliable, safe and affordable enough for widespread commercial deployment.

Nine different robotic systems will be demonstrated, including humanoid machines from Chinese manufacturers Unitree and AGIBOT, four-legged robots, mobile platforms and intelligent robotic arms.

Hosted by German engineering group FEV, the two-day event will examine physical AI, which allows machines to interpret and respond to their surroundings, and the technical advances needed to make increasingly autonomous robots practical for factories and other workplaces.

Among those taking part are experts from NEURA Robotics, Hugging Face, Schaeffler, Infineon Technologies, Humanoid, Synapticon, Wandelbots, Enchanted Tools, Sereact and the Fraunhofer Institute for Manufacturing Engineering and Automation.

The programme will cover robots capable of learning new tasks, advances in sensors and control systems, and the challenge of integrating intelligent machines into existing industrial operations.

Europe’s ability to compete in the developing global humanoid robotics market will also be examined at the event held in Aachen on 25 and 26 November.

Dr Dominik Lückmann, the chief innovation officer at FEV Group, said: “The value of a robot ultimately depends on its ability to perform a specific task reliably and at an economically viable cost.

“To achieve this, artificial intelligence, hardware, and system integration must work together seamlessly.”

Investment in humanoid robotics has surged, with $2.65 billion invested in start-ups worldwide in 2025, according to figures reported by the International Federation of Robotics.

But despite the investment, commercial adoption remains limited, with manufacturers still confronting problems involving cost, reliability, dexterity and safety.

Many advanced humanoid systems remain in development or are undergoing industrial trials, experts say.

Lückmann added: “With ARC, we bring together developers, suppliers, and end users to discuss the key challenges that need to be overcome for the widespread adoption of humanoid robotics.”
